1	# T03c Audit the published file against the closed ledger and write the outputs — AC-2, AC-7
2	Context: T03a and T03b read a county and close its ledger (values accepted only when their two printed sums hold). This task compares it with the published file, settles each disagreement with the printed totals, and writes what a maintainer needs: findings with evidence, a corrected file, a diff and a report. Repo root, branch main, BASE: the commit `pb.py task T03c start` recorded.
3	Read first: AGENTS.md, ARCHITECTURE.md (The audit, Outputs), .prod-build/contract.md#9-acceptance-criteria, crossfoot/agent.py, crossfoot/outputs.py, crossfoot/checks.py, crossfoot/ledger.py, crossfoot/sources.py, .prod-build/reports/T03b.md, the newest `runs/<run_id>/panola/county.json`
4	Memory to apply: run `python3 .prod-build/pb.py mem find --terms audit` first.
5	
6	Done when (REQUIRED): `uv run crossfoot audit --county panola` reads the county (reader chosen by measurement), closes it (the loop), compares the ledger with the published file and writes `runs/<run_id>/panola/findings.json`, `crops/*.png`, `corrected/20241105__tx__general__panola__precinct.csv`, `changes.diff` and `report.md` next to `county.json`; `--resume <run_id>` and `--resume latest` reuse a ledger instead of reading again; `uv run crossfoot verify-known --county panola` passes; `uv run pytest -q` passes.
7	
8	What the published file looks like (`data/files/panola.csv`, 783 rows; look at it yourself): columns `county, precinct, office, district, party, candidate, votes, absentee, early_voting, election_day`. "Registered Voters" rows carry only `votes`; "Ballots Cast" rows carry the parts. Labels differ from the scan's: the scan prints a ticket ("A/B (PARTY)") or "Write In" above a name, the file has one name and a party column; capitals and spellings vary, and one office name appears in two spellings. Some contests on the last page cover only some precincts (the scan blacks out the other cells and the file has rows only for some precincts, with a `district` value). EARLY is `early_voting`, ABSENTEE is `absentee`, PRECINCT is `election_day`, the small total under a column is `votes`.
9	
10	Carried over from the last task (do these first, each is small):
11	- The 22 cells of the registered-voters row are left `first_read` although their only sum ended with the verdict `cannot_verify`. Every value has to end as `accepted`, `document_inconsistent` or `cannot_verify` (AC-1): give them the verdict's status and reason.
12	- 76 cells of page 1's first block (registered voters and ballots cast) have no box in `county.json`, so they cannot be cropped or drawn. Work their boxes out from that block's ruled lines the way the other blocks do, and check two of them by eye on a crop.
13	- `run.json` of a close has no seconds and no reader; `audit` writes one `run.json` for the whole command with started, ended, seconds, reader, the sample's figures, model calls by model, tokens and metered cost.
14	
15	Acceptance (REQUIRED):
16	- WHEN the audit runs THE SYSTEM SHALL match contests and candidates by normalised labels first, send only what is left to the model once per county as two lists, and check the answer in code (one-to-one; mapped pairs have close county totals); what cannot be matched is listed, never guessed
17	- The published file is a second reading of the same scan, and the audit uses it to know where to look, never what to write. WHEN a published value differs from the ledger's value THE SYSTEM SHALL look at that value on the scan once more (the loop's single-value re-read at 400 dpi or more, with `claude-sonnet-4.6`) before anything is concluded: IF the re-read gives the file's value and the sums hold with it THEN the ledger was wrong, the value is corrected with an event and there is no finding; IF it gives the ledger's value again THEN the finding stands. Re-reads may run up to three at a time with call starts at least 1.1 seconds apart.
18	- WHEN a published value still disagrees after that THE SYSTEM SHALL write a finding with: county, office, candidate, precinct, part (`votes`, `absentee`, `early_voting` or `election_day`), file value, scan value, kind (`file_row_fails_own_total`, `wrong_number`, `wrong_column`, `wrong_precinct`, `missing_row`, `extra_row`), status, the sums that decide it (each with its terms, the printed total, and whether it holds with the file's value and with the scan's value), page, block, the cell's box, the crop path, and `confirmed_by_person: false`
19	- Status rules, in code and tested: `settled_against_file` only when at least one printed total on the scan holds with the scan's value and fails with the file's value, and no printed total holds with the file's value and fails with the scan's; `document_inconsistent` when the scan's own printed totals disagree with each other at that cell (name which); `cannot_verify` when no printed total decides (a sum that fails with both values decides nothing) or the scan's value itself is in doubt. The row totals and the grand total count as printed totals: a small total that is hard to read is decided by them.
20	- AC-7: WHEN the corrected file is written THE SYSTEM SHALL change only cells whose finding is `settled_against_file`, keep every other byte of the published file, and write `changes.diff` (unified) for exactly those lines (tested with a small made-up file and ledger)
21	- Findings that describe one slip are grouped: a value sitting in the wrong part of the same precinct is one `wrong_column` group; the same values sitting under other precincts of the same row is one `wrong_precinct` group; give each group an id and keep the cell-level findings under it
22	- A published row whose own parts do not add to its `votes` is a `file_row_fails_own_total` finding whether or not the scan decides it; then the rules above give its status
23	- AC-2: `uv run crossfoot verify-known --county panola` compares the newest `findings.json` with `tests/known_panola.json` and exits non-zero if an expected finding is missing; it prints how many findings were expected, how many were found, and how many findings there are in all. The audit code must not read that file (a test checks that no module under `crossfoot/` except the `verify-known` command names it).
24	- `report.md`: plain words; counts by kind and status; then one section per group with the crop, the sums in words and numbers, the file's value and the scan's value; then what could not be verified and why. Follow the wording rule in AGENTS.md: these are transcription slips in a volunteer dataset, the scan is the source, no comment on any candidate, party or official, and nothing says a person has confirmed a finding.
25	- Policy (`policy.py`): one question, id `document_disagrees_with_itself`; the default answer is "follow the cells as printed and list the printed total as inconsistent", stored in `runs/<run_id>/policy.json` with `answered_by: "default, not yet confirmed by a person"`; `crossfoot policy set --answer cells|totals` stores a person's answer for later runs.

# Architecture

Crossfoot is one Python package with a command-line entry point, files on disk, and a static results page. No
server, no database server, no queue. Each part below names the requirement in `.prod-build/contract.md` that forces it.

## The idea in one paragraph

A scanned table prints its own totals. If every cell is read into a ledger, each value can be tested twice: its
row has to add up to the total printed at the end of the row, and its column has to add up to the total printed
under the column. One wrong cell fails both sums, and the two failing sums cross at it. Crossfoot reads the scan
with a vision model, accepts a value only when both sums hold, re-reads the cells where they do not, and then uses
the closed ledger to audit a published file that was copied from the same scan.

## Layout of the repository

```
crossfoot/
  cli.py        command-line entry point (argparse): audit, read, verify-known, budget, site
  sources.py    the eight benchmark counties: scan URL, published-file URL, cache under data/ (M1, M4)
  render.py     pdftoppm wrapper: page -> PNG at a dpi; crops with Pillow (M1, M3)
  segment.py    finds blocks and column lines on a ruled page from the image itself (M1)
  model.py      gateway client, JSON parsing with one repair attempt, cost meter, budget guard, rate limit (M7)
  tracing.py    neatlogs setup and span helpers; a no-op when the key is absent (M7)
  layouts/
    matrix.py   precincts as columns, three rows per candidate, totals both ways (Panola)
    report.py   one precinct per page, one row per candidate with its own total (San Saba, Cottle and others)
    profile.py  decides which layout a county uses and tests the decision on the first pages (M1)
  ledger.py     SQLite ledger: cells, printed totals, checks, events; resume (M2, M6)
  checks.py     row sums, column sums, grand totals, grid completeness; pure functions (M2)
  agent.py      the investigation loop: a model chooses the next action for each open item; code enforces the rules (M3)
  audit.py      compares the closed ledger with the published file; classifies and settles disagreements (M4)
  outputs.py    county.json, findings.json, corrected CSV, report.md, the site's data bundle (M5, M8)
  policy.py     the one stored answer and its default (S1)
tests/          unit tests for checks, ledger, audit, budget, resume, agent rules; no network
site/           the static results page (plain HTML, CSS and JS; no build step) (M8)
runs/           one folder per run; small results are committed, caches are not
data/           downloaded scans and files; never committed
```

## Inputs

Eight Texas counties from the OpenElections project's 2024 general election benchmark. All eight scans are
image-only PDFs (no text layer): Cottle 12 pages, Foard 16, Jones 20, Limestone 42, Lynn 37, Panola 6, San Saba 21,
Scurry 38.

- Scan: `https://raw.githubusercontent.com/openelections/openelections-sources-tx/master/2024/general/2024%20<County>%20County%2C%20TX%20precinct-level%20results.pdf`
- Published file: `https://raw.githubusercontent.com/openelections/openelections-data-tx/master/2024/counties/20241105__tx__general__<county>__precinct.csv`
  with columns `county, precinct, office, district, party, candidate, votes, absentee, early_voting, election_day`.

## Two layouts

**Matrix (Panola).** A landscape canvass sheet. The header row lists the precincts as columns and ends in a TOTAL
column. Each candidate is a block: a label at the left, three ruled rows (EARLY, ABSENTEE, PRECINCT), a row of
small printed totals under the columns, and a grand total under the TOTAL column. In the published file EARLY is
`early_voting`, ABSENTEE is `absentee`, PRECINCT is `election_day`, and the small total is `votes`.
Checks per block: for each precinct, early + absentee + precinct = the small total; for each row, the precinct cells
add to the row's TOTAL; the small totals add to the grand total.

**Report (San Saba, Cottle and others).** One precinct per page or section. Each candidate is a row with four
numbers: TOTAL, Absentee, Early Voting, Election Day. Checks per row: total = absentee + early + election day.
Where the page prints a total for the contest, the candidates' totals have to add to it.

`layouts/profile.py` asks the model which layout the first page shows and what the column order is, then reads the
first page under that layout and runs the checks. A profile under which more than a third of the sums fail is
rejected; the other layout is tried; if neither holds the county is reported as "layout not supported" and left alone.

## Reading

1. `render.py` renders a page at 200 dpi.
2. Matrix: `segment.py` finds the blocks as bands of ink separated by blank bands, and the column lines inside a
   block as columns of dark pixels that run the height of the ruled rows. Report: the page is read whole.
3. Matrix: each block is cut into column groups no wider than 1,500 px at 300 dpi, one model call per group; report:
   one page per call. The answer is strict JSON, validated (right number of columns, integers only), with one repair
   request. Every value comes back with the block, row kind and column it belongs to.
4. Which model reads a county is decided by measurement, not fixed. A sample of the first page is read with
   `claude-haiku`; if more than a tenth of the sample's row sums fail, the county is read with `claude-sonnet-4.6`.
   Measured on Panola on 11 October 2026, same code and crops: `claude-haiku` left 85 of 943 printed sums failing
   (44 after a 20-minute re-read loop with 565 more calls); `claude-sonnet-4.6` left 6 of 942.
5. The values go into the ledger as `first_read`, with the page and the pixel box of each value where it is known.

## The ledger (`ledger.py`, SQLite, one file per run)

- `cells(county, page, block_id, contest, candidate, row_kind, column, value, first_read, status, tries, model, x0, y0, x1, y1)`
  with status in `first_read | accepted | failed | cannot_verify`.
- `totals(county, page, block_id, direction, key, value)` for printed row totals, column totals and grand totals.
- `events(ts, county, kind, payload_json)` for everything the agent did, in order. The results page replays these.
- A county is `closed` when every sum holds and the grid has no gap, or every open cell is `cannot_verify`.
- Resume: on start, accepted cells are kept and only open ones are worked on.

## Checks (`checks.py`, no model, no I/O)

Pure functions over the ledger's rows. They return, for each sum, its terms, the printed total, the computed total
and pass or fail, and for each failing cell the sums that cross at it. `locate()` returns the cells that sit on a
failing row sum and a failing column sum at once. Grid completeness lists every precinct, contest and candidate that
is present in one place and absent in another.

## The investigation loop (`agent.py`)

Every value on a matrix sheet sits on two printed sums. A cell sits on its row and its column. The small total under
a column sits on that column and on the grand total (the small totals add to it). A row's printed total sits on its
row and on the grand total (the three row totals add to it). So one wrong value makes exactly two sums fail, and they
cross at it. `checks.suspects()` pairs failing sums that share one value and whose differences agree: that value is
the suspect, and the difference says what it would have to be. (The grand total is checked two ways, kinds `grand_col`
and `grand_row`. The registered-voters row of Panola sits on one sum only and cannot be located this way.)

The loop works the sums that still fail after the first read, and later every disagreement with the published file.
For a located suspect it looks at the scan again: a re-read of that one value, cut at 400 dpi or more and enlarged.
A value changes only because a re-read of the scan gave the new value; arithmetic says where to look, never what to
write. What pairing cannot locate goes to the model, which is shown the failing sums and what has been tried and
returns one action as JSON:

- `reread {target, dpi, model}`: a single value, a column slice or a row strip
- `conclude {item, verdict, reason}`: `document_inconsistent` or `cannot_verify`
- `ask_policy {question_id}`: use the stored answer, or the default marked as unconfirmed
- `done {item}`

Rules that code enforces whatever the model says: at most six actions per item; re-reads climb one step at a time
(the county's reader, then `claude-sonnet-4.6`, then `claude-opus-4.6`), a step only after the one below has failed
to settle the value; the same target is never re-read twice with the same model and dpi; no value is accepted unless
both of its sums hold; a value the scan shows the same way twice while its two sums still fail is
`document_inconsistent` (the document disagrees with itself there) and the stored policy answer applies; a correction
is written only when the printed totals agree with the new value and disagree with the old one.
Every action and its result is an event in the ledger and a span in neatlogs.

## The audit (`audit.py`)

1. Load the published file. Normalise labels (case, punctuation, party suffixes, running mates).
2. Map the scan's contests and candidates to the file's. Exact and normalised matches first; what is left goes to
   the model once per county as two lists, and code checks that the answer is one-to-one and that mapped pairs have
   close county totals.
3. Compare cell by cell. A disagreement is classified:
   `file_row_fails_own_total`, `wrong_number`, `wrong_column`, `wrong_precinct`, `missing_row`, `extra_row`.
4. Settle it. If the scan's value passes both of its sums and the file's value breaks a printed total, the status is
   `settled_against_file`. If no printed total can decide, `cannot_verify`. If the scan's own totals disagree with
   its cells, `document_inconsistent`, and the stored policy answer applies.
5. Keep the evidence: the crop of the block, the sums with their terms, the old and the new value.
   Every finding carries `confirmed_by_person: false` until a person changes it.

## Outputs (`outputs.py`)

`runs/<run_id>/run.json` (start, end, commit, model calls, tokens, cost, counties), and per county
`county.json` (cells, totals, checks, events), `findings.json`, `crops/*.png`, `corrected/<published file name>`,
`changes.diff` and `report.md`. `crossfoot site build --run <id>` copies what the results page needs into
`site/data/`: `index.json`, one JSON per county, the page images that carry findings (at most 1600 px wide) and the crops.

## Tracing and cost (`tracing.py`, `model.py`)

`neatlogs.init(api_key=..., workflow_name="crossfoot")`; the gateway client is wrapped with `neatlogs.wrap(OpenAI(...))`.
A county run is a `WORKFLOW` span, the loop is an `AGENT` span, each tool is a `TOOL` span
(`@neatlogs.span(kind="TOOL", tool_name=...)`), tagged with run, county, page, block and cell. `neatlogs.flush()` and
`neatlogs.shutdown()` run at exit. The cost meter adds up each response's token usage, and `crossfoot budget` reads
the gateway's own figure for the key (`GET <gateway root>/key/info`, where the root is `LITELLM_BASE_URL` without
`/v1`). The guard refuses a call that would pass the limit.

## The results page (`site/`)

Plain HTML, CSS and JavaScript modules, no framework and no build step, so it deploys as static files. It reads
`site/data/`. The scan is an image inside a container with CSS perspective; cells, sums and marks are DOM and SVG
elements placed in the image's own coordinates, so they tilt with it and stay real, selectable elements.
`UI-SPEC.md` is the specification.

## What can fail and what happens

| Dependency | Failure | What the program does |
|---|---|---|
| Model gateway | rate limit, timeout | waits and retries once, then marks the item cannot-verify |
| Model gateway | budget reached | stops before the call, writes what it has, exits with a clear message |
| Model answer | not valid JSON, wrong column count | one repair request, then the block is marked failed and goes to the loop |
| Scan or file | cannot be downloaded | that county stops with the URL; other counties continue |
| neatlogs | key missing or unreachable | the run continues untraced and says so on its first line |
| Position finding | no ruled lines | crops fall back to whole blocks and the page shows crops without cell marks |

## Decisions

- SQLite for the ledger, because a stopped run has to resume and the page replays events in order.
- A JSON action protocol for the loop instead of provider tool-calling, so it runs unchanged on any model the gateway serves.
- CSS 3D for the stage instead of WebGL: the sheet is the only object, text has to stay crisp and selectable, and
  the page has to work with the effect off.

from PIL import Image

from . import checks

LAYOUT = "matrix"
GEO_DPI = 200


def _page_sizes(county, pages, root=None):
    from .render import page_png
    from .sources import DATA
    root = root or DATA
    out = []
    for n in pages:
        try:
            with Image.open(page_png(county, n, GEO_DPI, root)) as im:
                out.append({"number": n, "width": im.width, "height": im.height, "dpi": GEO_DPI})
        except Exception:
            out.append({"number": n, "width": None, "height": None, "dpi": GEO_DPI})

def write_county(run_dir, county, run_id, led, geo, summary, *, pages=None, data_root=None) -> Path:
    cells, totals = led.cells(county), led.totals(county)
    if pages is None:
        pages = sorted({c["page"] for c in cells})
    box = lambda c: [c[k] for k in ("x0", "y0", "x1", "y1")] if c["x0"] is not None else None
    seen, blocks = set(), []
    for c in cells:
        k = (c["page"], c["block_id"])
        if k not in seen:
            seen.add(k)
            bb = geo.block_box(*k) if geo else None
            blocks.append({"id": c["block_id"], "page": c["page"], "contest": c["contest"],
                           "candidate": c["candidate"], "box": list(bb) if bb else None})
    chs = [{"kind": ch.kind, "page": ch.page, "block": ch.block_id, "key": ch.key,
            "terms": [list(k) for k, _ in ch.terms], "printed": ch.printed, "computed": ch.computed, "ok": ch.ok,
            "note": ch.note} for ch in checks.all_checks(cells, totals)]
    evs = led.events(county)
    chosen = next((json.loads(e["payload_json"]) for e in reversed(evs) if e["kind"] == "choose_reader"), None)
    tbox = lambda t: (lambda b: list(b) if b else None)(
        geo.total_box(t["page"], t["block_id"], t["direction"], t["key"]) if geo else None)
    d = {"county": county, "run_id": run_id, "layout": LAYOUT,
         "pages": _page_sizes(county, pages, data_root) if pages else [],
         "blocks": blocks,
         "cells": [{"page": c["page"], "block": c["block_id"], "contest": c["contest"], "candidate": c["candidate"],
                    "row_kind": c["row_kind"], "column": c["column"], "value": c["value"],
                    "first_read": c["first_read"], "status": c["status"], "tries": c["tries"], "model": c["model"],
                    "reason": c.get("reason"), "box": box(c)} for c in cells],
         "totals": [{"page": t["page"], "block": t["block_id"], "direction": t["direction"], "key": t["key"],
                     "value": t["value"], "box": tbox(t)} for t in totals],
         "checks": chs,
         "reader": (chosen or {}).get("reader") or summary.get("reader"),
         "sample": chosen,
         "verdicts": [{"sum": v["sum_id"], "page": v["page"], "block": v["block_id"], "verdict": v["verdict"],
                       "reason": v["reason"], "entity": json.loads(v["entity"]) if v["entity"] else None}
                      for v in led.verdicts(county)],
         "events": [{"ts": e["ts"], "kind": e["kind"], "payload": json.loads(e["payload_json"])} for e in evs],
         "summary": summary}
    out = Path(run_dir) / county / "county.json"
    out.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    out.write_text(json.dumps(d, separators=(",", ":")))   # no indentation: it was 2.3 MB with
    return out


def git_commit() -> str | None:
    try:
        return subprocess.run(["git", "rev-parse", "HEAD"], capture_output=True, text=True, check=True).stdout.strip()
    except (OSError, subprocess.CalledProcessError):
        return None


def write_run(run_dir, run_id, *, started, ended, command, counties, gw, resumed_from=None) -> Path:
    d = {"run_id": run_id, "started": started, "ended": ended, "commit": git_commit(), "command": command,
         "counties": counties, "resumed_from": resumed_from, "model_calls": gw.calls,
         "prompt_tokens": gw.prompt_tokens, "completion_tokens": gw.completion_tokens,
         "metered_cost_estimate": round(gw.cost, 4)}
    out = Path(run_dir) / "run.json"
    out.write_text(json.dumps(d, indent=1))
    return out
"""SQLite ledger: cells, printed totals and events for one run. Resume keeps accepted cells."""
from __future__ import annotations

import json
import sqlite3
import time
from pathlib import Path

SCHEMA = """
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS cells(
  id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, county TEXT, page INTEGER, block_id TEXT, contest TEXT, candidate TEXT,
  row_kind TEXT, column TEXT, value INTEGER, first_read INTEGER, status TEXT DEFAULT 'first_read',
  tries INTEGER DEFAULT 0, model TEXT, x0 INTEGER, y0 INTEGER, x1 INTEGER, y1 INTEGER, reason TEXT,
  UNIQUE(county, page, block_id, row_kind, column));
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS totals(
  county TEXT, page INTEGER, block_id TEXT, direction TEXT, key TEXT, value INTEGER,
  UNIQUE(county, page, block_id, direction, key));
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS verdicts(
  county TEXT, sum_id TEXT, page INTEGER, block_id TEXT, verdict TEXT, reason TEXT, entity TEXT,
  UNIQUE(county, sum_id));
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS events(
  id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, ts REAL, county TEXT, kind TEXT, payload_json TEXT);
"""
STATUSES = ("first_read", "accepted", "failed", "cannot_verify", "document_inconsistent")
VERDICTS = ("document_inconsistent", "cannot_verify")


class Ledger:
    """One SQLite file. Cells are keyed by (county, page, block_id, row_kind, column)."""

    def __init__(self, path: str | Path = ":memory:"):
        self.db = sqlite3.connect(str(path))
        self.db.row_factory = sqlite3.Row
        self.db.executescript(SCHEMA)
        if "reason" not in {r["name"] for r in self.db.execute("PRAGMA table_info(cells)")}:
            self.db.execute("ALTER TABLE cells ADD COLUMN reason TEXT")  # ledgers made before the loop existed

    def close(self):
        self.db.close()

    def put_cell(self, county, page, block_id, row_kind, column, value, *, contest=None, candidate=None,
                 model=None, box=(None, None, None, None)):
        """Insert a first read, or re-read an open cell. An accepted cell is never overwritten (resume)."""
        self.db.execute(
            "INSERT INTO cells(county,page,block_id,contest,candidate,row_kind,column,value,first_read,model,x0,y0,x1,y1)"
            " VALUES(?,?,?,?,?,?,?,?,?,?,?,?,?,?)"
            " ON CONFLICT(county,page,block_id,row_kind,column) DO UPDATE SET value=excluded.value,"
            " tries=tries+1, model=excluded.model WHERE status!='accepted'",
            (county, page, block_id, contest, candidate, row_kind, column, value, value, model, *box))
        self.db.commit()

    def set_status(self, county, page, block_id, row_kind, column, status, reason=None):
        if status not in STATUSES:
            raise ValueError(f"unknown status {status!r}")
        self.db.execute("UPDATE cells SET status=?, reason=? WHERE county=? AND page=? AND block_id=? AND row_kind=? "
                        "AND column=?", (status, reason, county, page, block_id, row_kind, column))
        self.db.commit()

    def reread_cell(self, county, page, block_id, row_kind, column, value, model=None):
        """Record one re-read of a cell: tries goes up by one, the value is the one kept, the model only if it changed it."""
        self.db.execute("UPDATE cells SET value=?, tries=tries+1, model=COALESCE(?, model) WHERE county=? AND page=? "
                        "AND block_id=? AND row_kind=? AND column=? AND status!='accepted'",
                        (value, model, county, page, block_id, row_kind, column))
        self.db.commit()

    def put_total(self, county, page, block_id, direction, key, value):
        self.db.execute("INSERT OR REPLACE INTO totals VALUES(?,?,?,?,?,?)",
                        (county, page, block_id, direction, key, value))
        self.db.commit()

    def set_verdict(self, county, sum_id, page, block_id, verdict, reason, entity=None):
        """A failing sum that was worked and could not be made to hold: its verdict and why. One per sum."""
        if verdict not in VERDICTS:
            raise ValueError(f"unknown verdict {verdict!r}")
        self.db.execute("INSERT OR REPLACE INTO verdicts VALUES(?,?,?,?,?,?,?)",
                        (county, sum_id, page, block_id, verdict, reason, json.dumps(entity) if entity else None))
        self.db.commit()

    def verdicts(self, county=None) -> list[dict]:
        q, a = "SELECT * FROM verdicts", []
        if county:
            q += " WHERE county=?"; a.append(county)
        return [dict(r) for r in self.db.execute(q, a)]

    def clear_values(self, county):
        """Forget every cell and printed total of a county (the sample of a read that chose another reader). Events stay."""
        self.db.execute("DELETE FROM cells WHERE county=?", (county,))
        self.db.execute("DELETE FROM totals WHERE county=?", (county,))
        self.db.commit()

    def event(self, county, kind, payload=None):
        self.db.execute("INSERT INTO events(ts,county,kind,payload_json) VALUES(?,?,?,?)",
                        (time.time(), county, kind, json.dumps(payload or {})))
        self.db.commit()

    def cells(self, county=None, status=None) -> list[dict]:
        q, a = "SELECT * FROM cells WHERE 1=1", []
        if county:
            q += " AND county=?"; a.append(county)
        if status:
            q += " AND status=?"; a.append(status)
        return [dict(r) for r in self.db.execute(q + " ORDER BY id", a)]

    def totals(self, county=None) -> list[dict]:
        q, a = "SELECT * FROM totals", []
        if county:
            q += " WHERE county=?"; a.append(county)
        return [dict(r) for r in self.db.execute(q, a)]

    def events(self, county=None) -> list[dict]:
        q, a = "SELECT * FROM events", []
        if county:
            q += " WHERE county=?"; a.append(county)
        return [dict(r) for r in self.db.execute(q + " ORDER BY id", a)]

    def open_cells(self, county=None) -> list[dict]:
        """Cells that still need work: first_read or failed."""
        return [c for c in self.cells(county) if c["status"] in ("first_read", "failed")]

class FetchError(Exception):
    """A download failed; the message carries the URL."""


def scan_url(key: str) -> str:
    return _SCAN.format(name=quote(COUNTIES[key]))


def file_url(key: str) -> str:
    return _FILE.format(key=key)

    return root / "scans" / f"{key}.pdf"


def file_path(key: str, root: Path = DATA) -> Path:
    return root / "files" / f"{key}.csv"


def _download(url: str, dest: Path) -> bool:
    """Download url to dest unless dest exists. Returns True if a download happened."""
    if dest.exists() and dest.stat().st_size > 0:
        return False
    dest.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    part = dest.with_suffix(dest.suffix + ".part")
    try:
        with urllib.request.urlopen(url, timeout=60) as r, open(part, "wb") as f:
            while chunk := r.read(1 << 16):
                f.write(chunk)
    except (urllib.error.URLError, OSError, TimeoutError) as e:
        part.unlink(missing_ok=True)
        raise FetchError(f"could not download {url}: {e}") from e
    os.replace(part, dest)
    return True


def fetch(key: str, root: Path = DATA) -> list[str]:
    """Make sure the scan and the published file of one county are cached. Returns the names downloaded now."""
    got = []
    if _download(scan_url(key), scan_path(key, root)):
        got.append("scan")
    if _download(file_url(key), file_path(key, root)):
        got.append("file")
    return got


def read_published(key: str, root: Path = DATA) -> list[dict]:
    with open(file_path(key, root), newline="", encoding="utf-8") as f:
        return list(csv.DictReader(f))

    s = (s or "").strip().replace(",", "")
    try:
        return int(s)
    except ValueError:
        return None

    """Rows whose votes differ from absentee + early_voting + election_day.

    Returns (bad rows, rows checked, rows skipped because votes or a part is blank or not a number).
    Each bad row is the original dict plus a `parts_sum` key.

    bad, checked, skipped = [], 0, 0
    for r in rows:
        vals = [_int(r.get(c)) for c in ("votes", "absentee", "early_voting", "election_day")]

            bad.append({**r, "parts_sum": total})
    return bad, checked, skipped

result.output:
## Inputs

Eight Texas counties from the OpenElections project's 2024 general election benchmark. All eight scans are
image-only PDFs (no text layer): Cottle 12 pages, Foard 16, Jones 20, Limestone 42, Lynn 37, Panola 6, San Saba 21,
Scurry 38.

- Scan: `https://raw.githubusercontent.com/openelections/openelections-sources-tx/master/2024/general/2024%20<County>%20County%2C%20TX%20precinct-level%20results.pdf`
- Published file: `https://raw.githubusercontent.com/openelections/openelections-data-tx/master/2024/counties/20241105__tx__general__<county>__precinct.csv`
  with columns `county, precinct, office, district, party, candidate, votes, absentee, early_voting, election_day`.

## Two layouts

**Matrix (Panola).** A landscape canvass sheet. The header row lists the precincts as columns and ends in a TOTAL
column. Each candidate is a block: a label at the left, three ruled rows (EARLY, ABSENTEE, PRECINCT), a row of
small printed totals under the columns, and a grand total under the TOTAL column. In the published file EARLY is
`early_voting`, ABSENTEE is `absentee`, PRECINCT is `election_day`, and the small total is `votes`.
Checks per block: for each precinct, early + absentee + precinct = the small total; for each row, the precinct cells
add to the row's TOTAL; the small totals add to the grand total.

**Report (San Saba, Cottle and others).** One precinct per page or section. Each candidate is a row with four
numbers: TOTAL, Absentee, Early Voting, Election Day. Checks per row: total = absentee + early + election day.
Where the page prints a total for the contest, the candidates' totals have to add to it.

`layouts/profile.py` asks the model which layout the first page shows and what the column order is, then reads the
first page under that layout and runs the checks. A profile under which more than a third of the sums fail is
rejected; the other layout is tried; if neither holds the county is reported as "layout not supported" and left alone.

## Reading

1. `render.py` renders a page at 200 dpi.
2. Matrix: `segment.py` finds the blocks as bands of ink separated by blank bands, and the column lines inside a
   block as columns of dark pixels that run the height of the ruled rows. Report: the page is read whole.
3. Matrix: each block is cut into column groups no wider than 1,500 px at 300 dpi, one model call per group; report:
   one page per call. The answer is strict JSON, validated (right number of columns, integers only), with one repair
   request. Every value comes back with the block, row kind and column it belongs to.
4. Which model reads a county is decided by measurement, not fixed. A sample of the first page is read with
   `claude-haiku`; if more than a tenth of the sample's row sums fail, the county is read with `claude-sonnet-4.6`.
   Measured on Panola on 11 October 2026, same code and crops: `claude-haiku` left 85 of 943 printed sums failing
   (44 after a 20-minute re-read loop with 565 more calls); `claude-sonnet-4.6` left 6 of 942.
5. The values go into the ledger as `first_read`, with the page and the pixel box of each value where it is known.

## The ledger (`ledger.py`, SQLite, one file per run)

- `cells(county, page, block_id, contest, candidate, row_kind, column, value, first_read, status, tries, model, x0, y0, x1, y1)`
  with status in `first_read | accepted | failed | cannot_verify`.
- `totals(county, page, block_id, direction, key, value)` for printed row totals, column totals and grand totals.
- `events(ts, county, kind, payload_json)` for everything the agent did, in order. The results page replays these.
- A county is `closed` when every sum holds and the grid has no gap, or every open cell is `cannot_verify`.
- Resume: on start, accepted cells are kept and only open ones are worked on.

## Checks (`checks.py`, no model, no I/O)

Pure functions over the ledger's rows. They return, for each sum, its terms, the printed total, the computed total
and pass or fail, and for each failing cell the sums that cross at it. `locate()` returns the cells that sit on a
failing row sum and a failing column sum at once. Grid completeness lists every precinct, contest and candidate that
is present in one place and absent in another.

## The investigation loop (`agent.py`)

Every value on a matrix sheet sits on two printed sums. A cell sits on its row and its column. The small total under
a column sits on that column and on the grand total (the small totals add to it). A row's printed total sits on its
row and on the grand total (the three row totals add to it). So one wrong value makes exactly two sums fail, and they
cross at it. `checks.suspects()` pairs failing sums that share one value and whose differences agree: that value is
the suspect, and the difference says what it would have to be. (The grand total is checked two ways, kinds `grand_col`
and `grand_row`. The registered-voters row of Panola sits on one sum only and cannot be located this way.)

The loop works the sums that still fail after the first read, and later every disagreement with the published file.
For a located suspect it looks at the scan again: a re-read of that one value, cut at 400 dpi or more and enlarged.
A value changes only because a re-read of the scan gave the new value; arithmetic says where to look, never what to
write. What pairing cannot locate goes to the model, which is shown the failing sums and what has been tried and
returns one action as JSON:

- `reread {target, dpi, model}`: a single value, a column slice or a row strip
- `conclude {item, verdict, reason}`: `document_inconsistent` or `cannot_verify`
- `ask_policy {question_id}`: use the stored answer, or the default marked as unconfirmed
- `done {item}`

Rules that code enforces whatever the model says: at most six actions per item; re-reads climb one step at a time
(the county's reader, then `claude-sonnet-4.6`, then `claude-opus-4.6`), a step only after the one below has failed
to settle the value; the same target is never re-read twice with the same model and dpi; no value is accepted unless
both of its sums hold; a value the scan shows the same way twice while its two sums still fail is
`document_inconsistent` (the document disagrees with itself there) and the stored policy answer applies; a correction
is written only when the printed totals agree with the new value and disagree with the old one.
Every action and its result is an event in the ledger and a span in neatlogs.

## The audit (`audit.py`)

1. Load the published file. Normalise labels (case, punctuation, party suffixes, running mates).
2. Map the scan's contests and candidates to the file's. Exact and normalised matches first; what is left goes to
   the model once per county as two lists, and code checks that the answer is one-to-one and that mapped pairs have
   close county totals.
3. Compare cell by cell. A disagreement is classified:
   `file_row_fails_own_total`, `wrong_number`, `wrong_column`, `wrong_precinct`, `missing_row`, `extra_row`.
4. Settle it. If the scan's value passes both of its sums and the file's value breaks a printed total, the status is
   `settled_against_file`. If no printed total can decide, `cannot_verify`. If the scan's own totals disagree with
   its cells, `document_inconsistent`, and the stored policy answer applies.
5. Keep the evidence: the crop of the block, the sums with their terms, the old and the new value.
   Every finding carries `confirmed_by_person: false` until a person changes it.

## Outputs (`outputs.py`)

`runs/<run_id>/run.json` (start, end, commit, model calls, tokens, cost, counties), and per county
`county.json` (cells, totals, checks, events), `findings.json`, `crops/*.png`, `corrected/<published file name>`,
`changes.diff` and `report.md`. `crossfoot site build --run <id>` copies what the results page needs into
`site/data/`: `index.json`, one JSON per county, the page images that carry findings (at most 1600 px wide) and the crops.

## Tracing and cost (`tracing.py`, `model.py`)

`neatlogs.init(api_key=..., workflow_name="crossfoot")`; the gateway client is wrapped with `neatlogs.wrap(OpenAI(...))`.
A county run is a `WORKFLOW` span, the loop is an `AGENT` span, each tool is a `TOOL` span
(`@neatlogs.span(kind="TOOL", tool_name=...)`), tagged with run, county, page, block and cell. `neatlogs.flush()` and
`neatlogs.shutdown()` run at exit. The cost meter adds up each response's token usage, and `crossfoot budget` reads
the gateway's own figure for the key (`GET <gateway root>/key/info`, where the root is `LITELLM_BASE_URL` without
`/v1`). The guard refuses a call that would pass the limit.

## The results page (`site/`)

Plain HTML, CSS and JavaScript modules, no framework and no build step, so it deploys as static files. It reads
`site/data/`. The scan is an image inside a container with CSS perspective; cells, sums and marks are DOM and SVG
elements placed in the image's own coordinates, so they tilt with it and stay real, selectable elements.
`UI-SPEC.md` is the specification.

## What can fail and what happens

| Dependency | Failure | What the program does |
|---|---|---|
| Model gateway | rate limit, timeout | waits and retries once, then marks the item cannot-verify |
| Model gateway | budget reached | stops before the call, writes what it has, exits with a clear message |
| Model answer | not valid JSON, wrong column count | one repair request, then the block is marked failed and goes to the loop |
| Scan or file | cannot be downloaded | that county stops with the URL; other counties continue |
| neatlogs | key missing or unreachable | the run continues untraced and says so on its first line |
| Position finding | no ruled lines | crops fall back to whole blocks and the page shows crops without cell marks |

## Decisions

- SQLite for the ledger, because a stopped run has to resume and the page replays events in order.
- A JSON action protocol for the loop instead of provider tool-calling, so it runs unchanged on any model the gateway serves.
- CSS 3D for the stage instead of WebGL: the sheet is the only object, text has to stay crisp and selectable, and
  the page has to work with the effect off.

import json
import subprocess
from pathlib import Path

from PIL import Image

from . import checks

LAYOUT = "matrix"
GEO_DPI = 200


def _page_sizes(county, pages, root=None):
    from .render import page_png
    from .sources import DATA
    root = root or DATA
    out = []
    for n in pages:
        try:
            with Image.open(page_png(county, n, GEO_DPI, root)) as im:
                out.append({"number": n, "width": im.width, "height": im.height, "dpi": GEO_DPI})
        except Exception:
            out.append({"number": n, "width": None, "height": None, "dpi": GEO_DPI})
    return out


def write_county(run_dir, county, run_id, led, geo, summary, *, pages=None, data_root=None) -> Path:
    cells, totals = led.cells(county), led.totals(county)
    if pages is None:
        pages = sorted({c["page"] for c in cells})
    box = lambda c: [c[k] for k in ("x0", "y0", "x1", "y1")] if c["x0"] is not None else None
    seen, blocks = set(), []
    for c in cells:
        k = (c["page"], c["block_id"])
        if k not in seen:
            seen.add(k)
            bb = geo.block_box(*k) if geo else None
            blocks.append({"id": c["block_id"], "page": c["page"], "contest": c["contest"],
                           "candidate": c["candidate"], "box": list(bb) if bb else None})
    chs = [{"kind": ch.kind, "page": ch.page, "block": ch.block_id, "key": ch.key,
            "terms": [list(k) for k, _ in ch.terms], "printed": ch.printed, "computed": ch.computed, "ok": ch.ok,
            "note": ch.note} for ch in checks.all_checks(cells, totals)]
    evs = led.events(county)
    chosen = next((json.loads(e["payload_json"]) for e in reversed(evs) if e["kind"] == "choose_reader"), None)
    tbox = lambda t: (lambda b: list(b) if b else None)(
        geo.total_box(t["page"], t["block_id"], t["direction"], t["key"]) if geo else None)
    d = {"county": county, "run_id": run_id, "layout": LAYOUT,
         "pages": _page_sizes(county, pages, data_root) if pages else [],
         "blocks": blocks,
         "cells": [{"page": c["page"], "block": c["block_id"], "contest": c["contest"], "candidate": c["candidate"],
                    "row_kind": c["row_kind"], "column": c["column"], "value": c["value"],
                    "first_read": c["first_read"], "status": c["status"], "tries": c["tries"], "model": c["model"],
                    "reason": c.get("reason"), "box": box(c)} for c in cells],
         "totals": [{"page": t["page"], "block": t["block_id"], "direction": t["direction"], "key": t["key"],
                     "value": t["value"], "box": tbox(t)} for t in totals],
         "checks": chs,
         "reader": (chosen or {}).get("reader") or summary.get("reader"),
         "sample": chosen,
         "verdicts": [{"sum": v["sum_id"], "page": v["page"], "block": v["block_id"], "verdict": v["verdict"],
                       "reason": v["reason"], "entity": json.loads(v["entity"]) if v["entity"] else None}
                      for v in led.verdicts(county)],
         "events": [{"ts": e["ts"], "kind": e["kind"], "payload": json.loads(e["payload_json"])} for e in evs],
         "summary": summary}
    out = Path(run_dir) / county / "county.json"
    out.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    out.write_text(json.dumps(d, separators=(",", ":")))   # no indentation: it was 2.3 MB with
    return out


def git_commit() -> str | None:
    try:
        return subprocess.run(["git", "rev-parse", "HEAD"], capture_output=True, text=True, check=True).stdout.strip()
    except (OSError, subprocess.CalledProcessError):
        return None


def write_run(run_dir, run_id, *, started, ended, command, counties, gw, resumed_from=None) -> Path:
    d = {"run_id": run_id, "started": started, "ended": ended, "commit": git_commit(), "command": command,
         "counties": counties, "resumed_from": resumed_from, "model_calls": gw.calls,
         "prompt_tokens": gw.prompt_tokens, "completion_tokens": gw.completion_tokens,
         "metered_cost_estimate": round(gw.cost, 4)}
    out = Path(run_dir) / "run.json"
    out.write_text(json.dumps(d, indent=1))
    return out
"""SQLite ledger: cells, printed totals and events for one run. Resume keeps accepted cells."""
from __future__ import annotations

import json
import sqlite3
import time
from pathlib import Path

SCHEMA = """
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS cells(
  id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, county TEXT, page INTEGER, block_id TEXT, contest TEXT, candidate TEXT,
  row_kind TEXT, column TEXT, value INTEGER, first_read INTEGER, status TEXT DEFAULT 'first_read',
  tries INTEGER DEFAULT 0, model TEXT, x0 INTEGER, y0 INTEGER, x1 INTEGER, y1 INTEGER, reason TEXT,
  UNIQUE(county, page, block_id, row_kind, column));
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS totals(
  county TEXT, page INTEGER, block_id TEXT, direction TEXT, key TEXT, value INTEGER,
  UNIQUE(county, page, block_id, direction, key));
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS verdicts(
  county TEXT, sum_id TEXT, page INTEGER, block_id TEXT, verdict TEXT, reason TEXT, entity TEXT,
  UNIQUE(county, sum_id));
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS events(
  id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, ts REAL, county TEXT, kind TEXT, payload_json TEXT);
"""
STATUSES = ("first_read", "accepted", "failed", "cannot_verify", "document_inconsistent")
VERDICTS = ("document_inconsistent", "cannot_verify")


class Ledger:
    """One SQLite file. Cells are keyed by (county, page, block_id, row_kind, column)."""

    def __init__(self, path: str | Path = ":memory:"):
        self.db = sqlite3.connect(str(path))
        self.db.row_factory = sqlite3.Row
        self.db.executescript(SCHEMA)
        if "reason" not in {r["name"] for r in self.db.execute("PRAGMA table_info(cells)")}:
            self.db.execute("ALTER TABLE cells ADD COLUMN reason TEXT")  # ledgers made before the loop existed

    def close(self):
        self.db.close()

    def put_cell(self, county, page, block_id, row_kind, column, value, *, contest=None, candidate=None,
                 model=None, box=(None, None, None, None)):
        """Insert a first read, or re-read an open cell. An accepted cell is never overwritten (resume)."""
        self.db.execute(
            "INSERT INTO cells(county,page,block_id,contest,candidate,row_kind,column,value,first_read,model,x0,y0,x1,y1)"
            " VALUES(?,?,?,?,?,?,?,?,?,?,?,?,?,?)"
            " ON CONFLICT(county,page,block_id,row_kind,column) DO UPDATE SET value=excluded.value,"
            " tries=tries+1, model=excluded.model WHERE status!='accepted'",
            (county, page, block_id, contest, candidate, row_kind, column, value, value, model, *box))
        self.db.commit()

    def set_status(self, county, page, block_id, row_kind, column, status, reason=None):
        if status not in STATUSES:
            raise ValueError(f"unknown status {status!r}")
        self.db.execute("UPDATE cells SET status=?, reason=? WHERE county=? AND page=? AND block_id=? AND row_kind=? "
                        "AND column=?", (status, reason, county, page, block_id, row_kind, column))
        self.db.commit()

    def reread_cell(self, county, page, block_id, row_kind, column, value, model=None):
        """Record one re-read of a cell: tries goes up by one, the value is the one kept, the model only if it changed it."""
        self.db.execute("UPDATE cells SET value=?, tries=tries+1, model=COALESCE(?, model) WHERE county=? AND page=? "
                        "AND block_id=? AND row_kind=? AND column=? AND status!='accepted'",
                        (value, model, county, page, block_id, row_kind, column))
        self.db.commit()

    def put_total(self, county, page, block_id, direction, key, value):
        self.db.execute("INSERT OR REPLACE INTO totals VALUES(?,?,?,?,?,?)",
                        (county, page, block_id, direction, key, value))
        self.db.commit()

    def set_verdict(self, county, sum_id, page, block_id, verdict, reason, entity=None):
        """A failing sum that was worked and could not be made to hold: its verdict and why. One per sum."""
        if verdict not in VERDICTS:
            raise ValueError(f"unknown verdict {verdict!r}")
        self.db.execute("INSERT OR REPLACE INTO verdicts VALUES(?,?,?,?,?,?,?)",
                        (county, sum_id, page, block_id, verdict, reason, json.dumps(entity) if entity else None))
        self.db.commit()

    def verdicts(self, county=None) -> list[dict]:
        q, a = "SELECT * FROM verdicts", []
        if county:
            q += " WHERE county=?"; a.append(county)
        return [dict(r) for r in self.db.execute(q, a)]

    def clear_values(self, county):
        """Forget every cell and printed total of a county (the sample of a read that chose another reader). Events stay."""
        self.db.execute("DELETE FROM cells WHERE county=?", (county,))
        self.db.execute("DELETE FROM totals WHERE county=?", (county,))
        self.db.commit()

    def event(self, county, kind, payload=None):
        self.db.execute("INSERT INTO events(ts,county,kind,payload_json) VALUES(?,?,?,?)",
                        (time.time(), county, kind, json.dumps(payload or {})))
        self.db.commit()

    def cells(self, county=None, status=None) -> list[dict]:
        q, a = "SELECT * FROM cells WHERE 1=1", []
        if county:
            q += " AND county=?"; a.append(county)
        if status:
            q += " AND status=?"; a.append(status)
        return [dict(r) for r in self.db.execute(q + " ORDER BY id", a)]

    def totals(self, county=None) -> list[dict]:
        q, a = "SELECT * FROM totals", []
        if county:
            q += " WHERE county=?"; a.append(county)
        return [dict(r) for r in self.db.execute(q, a)]

    def events(self, county=None) -> list[dict]:
        q, a = "SELECT * FROM events", []
        if county:
            q += " WHERE county=?"; a.append(county)
        return [dict(r) for r in self.db.execute(q + " ORDER BY id", a)]

    def open_cells(self, county=None) -> list[dict]:
        """Cells that still need work: first_read or failed."""
        return [c for c in self.cells(county) if c["status"] in ("first_read", "failed")]
"""The eight benchmark counties: where their scan and published file live, and the local cache under data/."""
from __future__ import annotations

import csv
import os
import urllib.error
import urllib.request
from pathlib import Path
from urllib.parse import quote

DATA = Path("data")

COUNTIES = {
    "cottle": "Cottle",
    "foard": "Foard",
    "jones": "Jones",
    "limestone": "Limestone",
    "lynn": "Lynn",
    "panola": "Panola",
    "san_saba": "San Saba",
    "scurry": "Scurry",
}

_SCAN = ("https://raw.githubusercontent.com/openelections/openelections-sources-tx/master/2024/general/"
         "2024%20{name}%20County%2C%20TX%20precinct-level%20results.pdf")
_FILE = ("https://raw.githubusercontent.com/openelections/openelections-data-tx/master/2024/counties/"
         "20241105__tx__general__{key}__precinct.csv")


class FetchError(Exception):
    """A download failed; the message carries the URL."""


def scan_url(key: str) -> str:
    return _SCAN.format(name=quote(COUNTIES[key]))


def file_url(key: str) -> str:
    return _FILE.format(key=key)


def scan_path(key: str, root: Path = DATA) -> Path:
    return root / "scans" / f"{key}.pdf"


def file_path(key: str, root: Path = DATA) -> Path:
    return root / "files" / f"{key}.csv"


def _download(url: str, dest: Path) -> bool:
    """Download url to dest unless dest exists. Returns True if a download happened."""
    if dest.exists() and dest.stat().st_size > 0:
        return False
    dest.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    part = dest.with_suffix(dest.suffix + ".part")
    try:
        with urllib.request.urlopen(url, timeout=60) as r, open(part, "wb") as f:
            while chunk := r.read(1 << 16):
                f.write(chunk)
    except (urllib.error.URLError, OSError, TimeoutError) as e:
        part.unlink(missing_ok=True)
        raise FetchError(f"could not download {url}: {e}") from e
    os.replace(part, dest)
    return True


def fetch(key: str, root: Path = DATA) -> list[str]:
    """Make sure the scan and the published file of one county are cached. Returns the names downloaded now."""
    got = []
    if _download(scan_url(key), scan_path(key, root)):
        got.append("scan")
    if _download(file_url(key), file_path(key, root)):
        got.append("file")
    return got


def read_published(key: str, root: Path = DATA) -> list[dict]:
    with open(file_path(key, root), newline="", encoding="utf-8") as f:
        return list(csv.DictReader(f))


def _int(s: str | None) -> int | None:
    s = (s or "").strip().replace(",", "")
    try:
        return int(s)
    except ValueError:
        return None


def file_mismatches(rows: list[dict]) -> tuple[list[dict], int, int]:
    """Rows whose votes differ from absentee + early_voting + election_day.

    Returns (bad rows, rows checked, rows skipped because votes or a part is blank or not a number).
    Each bad row is the original dict plus a `parts_sum` key.
    """
    bad, checked, skipped = [], 0, 0
    for r in rows:
        vals = [_int(r.get(c)) for c in ("votes", "absentee", "early_voting", "election_day")]
        if any(v is None for v in vals):
            skipped += 1
            continue
        checked += 1
        total = vals[1] + vals[2] + vals[3]
        if vals[0] != total:
            bad.append({**r, "parts_sum": total})
    return bad, checked, skipped
"""Row sums, column sums and grid completeness. Pure functions: no I/O, no model.

Inputs are plain dicts as the ledger returns them. A cell needs `page, block_id, row_kind, column, value`
(value None means unread). A printed total is `page, block_id, direction, key, value` with direction
'row' (key = row_kind), 'col' (key = column) or 'grand' (key ignored).
A cell is identified by the tuple (page, block_id, row_kind, column), called a cell key below.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

from dataclasses import dataclass, field

ROW_TOTAL_COLUMN = "TOTAL"  # a cell in this column is the row's printed total, not a term


@dataclass
class Check:
    kind: str                 # 'row' | 'col' | 'grand_col' (small totals add to the grand total) | 'grand_row' (row totals do)
    page: int
    block_id: str
    key: str                  # row_kind for a row sum, column for a column sum, '' for grand
    terms: list = field(default_factory=list)  # [(cell key, value)]
    printed: int | None = None
    computed: int | None = None  # None when a term is unread
    ok: bool = False
    printed_key: tuple | None = None   # the printed total as a value of its own: (page, block, 'row'|'col'|'grand', key)
    note: str = ""                     # what is special about this sum (the registered-voters row sits on one sum only)


def cell_key(c: dict) -> tuple:
    return (c["page"], c["block_id"], c["row_kind"], c["column"])


def _printed(totals, direction):
    return {(t["page"], t["block_id"], t["key"] if direction != "grand" else ""): t["value"]
            for t in totals if t["direction"] == direction}


ONE_SUM = "registered voters: this row has no column sums, so its values sit on one sum only"


def _make(kind, page, block, key, cells, printed, printed_key=None, note="") -> Check:
    terms = [(cell_key(c), c["value"]) for c in cells]
    computed = None if any(v is None for _, v in terms) else sum(v for _, v in terms)
    return Check(kind, page, block, key, terms, printed, computed, computed is not None and computed == printed,
                 printed_key, note)


def row_checks(cells: list[dict], totals: list[dict]) -> list[Check]:
    """One check per (page, block, row_kind) that has a printed row total: the row's cells must add to it."""
    printed = _printed(totals, "row")
    groups: dict = {}
    for c in cells:
        if c["column"] != ROW_TOTAL_COLUMN:
            groups.setdefault((c["page"], c["block_id"], c["row_kind"]), []).append(c)
    return [_make("row", *k, g, printed[k], (k[0], k[1], "row", k[2]), ONE_SUM if k[2] == "REGISTERED" else "")
            for k, g in groups.items() if k in printed]


def column_checks(cells: list[dict], totals: list[dict]) -> list[Check]:
    """One check per (page, block, column) that has a printed column total: the column's cells must add to it."""
    printed = _printed(totals, "col")
    groups: dict = {}
    for c in cells:
        groups.setdefault((c["page"], c["block_id"], c["column"]), []).append(c)
    return [_make("col", *k, g, printed[k], (k[0], k[1], "col", k[2])) for k, g in groups.items() if k in printed]


def grand_checks(totals: list[dict]) -> list[Check]:
    """The printed column totals of a block must add to its printed grand total (kind 'grand_col')."""
    grand = _printed(totals, "grand")
    out = []
    for (page, block, _), g in grand.items():
        cols = [t for t in totals if t["direction"] == "col" and t["page"] == page and t["block_id"] == block]
        terms = [((page, block, "col", t["key"]), t["value"]) for t in cols]
        comp = sum(v for _, v in terms)
        out.append(Check("grand_col", page, block, "", terms, g, comp, comp == g, (page, block, "grand", "")))
    return out


def grand_row_checks(totals: list[dict]) -> list[Check]:
    """The printed row totals of a block must add to its printed grand total (kind 'grand_row'). The registered-voters
    row is not a term: it is not a count of ballots."""
    grand = _printed(totals, "grand")
    out = []
    for (page, block, _), g in grand.items():
        rows = [t for t in totals if t["direction"] == "row" and t["page"] == page and t["block_id"] == block and
                t["key"] != "REGISTERED"]
        if not rows:
            continue
        terms = [((page, block, "row", t["key"]), t["value"]) for t in rows]
        comp = sum(v for _, v in terms)
        out.append(Check("grand_row", page, block, "", terms, g, comp, comp == g, (page, block, "grand", "")))
    return out


def grid_gaps(cells: list[dict]) -> list[tuple]:
    """Cell keys that are absent or unread where the block's grid says they should be.

    Within a block the grid is every row_kind crossed with every column that appears in it.
    Returns sorted (page, block_id, row_kind, column) tuples.
    """
    blocks: dict = {}
    for c in cells:
        b = blocks.setdefault((c["page"], c["block_id"]), {"rows": set(), "cols": set(), "have": set()})
        b["rows"].add(c["row_kind"]); b["cols"].add(c["column"])
        if c["value"] is not None:
            b["have"].add((c["row_kind"], c["column"]))
    return sorted((p, bid, r, col) for (p, bid), b in blocks.items()
                  for r in b["rows"] for col in b["cols"] if (r, col) not in b["have"])


def locate(rows: list[Check], cols: list[Check]) -> list[tuple]:
    """Cell keys that sit on a failing row sum and on a failing column sum at once."""
    bad_rows = {k for ch in rows if not ch.ok for k, _ in ch.terms}
    bad_cols = {k for ch in cols if not ch.ok for k, _ in ch.terms}
    return sorted(bad_rows & bad_cols)


def all_checks(cells: list[dict], totals: list[dict]) -> list[Check]:
    return row_checks(cells, totals) + column_checks(cells, totals) + grand_checks(totals) + grand_row_checks(totals)


@dataclass
class Suspect:
    entity: tuple     # a cell key (page, block, row_kind, column) or a printed total (page, block, 'row'|'col'|'grand', key)
    read: int         # the value now in the ledger
    would_be: int     # the value both of its sums need
    error: int        # read - would_be
    sums: tuple       # the two failing Checks it sits on


@dataclass
class Located:
    suspects: list = field(default_factory=list)
    unlocated: list = field(default_factory=list)   # [(Check, why)]: failing sums no single value explains


def suspects(chs: list[Check]) -> Located:
    """Pair failing sums. A value that sits on exactly two failing sums, and is off by the same amount on both (the sign
    its place in each sum gives), is a suspect, and the value both sums need is `would_be`. A value read too high by e
    makes a sum it is a term of too high by e, and a sum it is the printed total of too low by e. Pure arithmetic:
    it says where to look, never what to write. A failing sum that no unique suspect explains is `unlocated`, with the
    reason (an unread term, one sum only, more than one candidate, or differences that do not pair)."""
    failing = [c for c in chs if not c.ok]
    out = Located()
    on: dict = {}                                  # entity -> [(Check, error it implies, value)]
    unread = []
    for c in failing:
        if c.computed is None or c.printed is None:
            unread.append(c)
            continue
        d = c.computed - c.printed
        for k, v in c.terms:
            on.setdefault(k, []).append((c, d, v))
        if c.printed_key is not None:
            on.setdefault(c.printed_key, []).append((c, -d, c.printed))
    cand = []
    for e, lst in on.items():
        if len(lst) == 2 and lst[0][1] == lst[1][1] != 0 and lst[0][2] - lst[0][1] >= 0:
            cand.append(Suspect(e, lst[0][2], lst[0][2] - lst[0][1], lst[0][1], (lst[0][0], lst[1][0])))
    uses: dict = {}
    for s in cand:
        for c in s.sums:
            uses[id(c)] = uses.get(id(c), 0) + 1
    out.suspects = [s for s in cand if all(uses[id(c)] == 1 for c in s.sums)]
    explained = {id(c) for s in out.suspects for c in s.sums}
    for c in failing:
        if id(c) in explained:
            continue
        if c in unread:
            why = "a term is unread"
        elif c.note:
            why = f"one sum only: {c.note}"
        elif uses.get(id(c), 0) > 1:
            why = "more than one value could be the one: several pairs of failing sums agree"
        else:
            why = "its difference cannot be paired with another failing sum (two or more wrong values may share it)"
        out.unlocated.append((c, why))
    return out


def crossing(cells: list[dict], totals: list[dict]) -> dict:
    """For each cell key, the row and column checks it sits on (a cell on no printed sum maps to an empty list)."""
    on: dict = {cell_key(c): [] for c in cells if c["column"] != ROW_TOTAL_COLUMN}
    for ch in row_checks(cells, totals) + column_checks(cells, totals):
        for k, _ in ch.terms:
            on[k].append(ch)
    return on

"""The investigation loop: pairing finds where to look, re-reads of the scan decide, code holds it to the rules.

Every printed value sits on two sums (see `checks.suspects`). A value that sits on two failing sums whose differences
agree is a suspect: it is re-read at 400 dpi or more with the county's reader, then one step up the ladder, and the
value changes only because a re-read gave the value both sums need. The same reading twice while both sums still
fail is `document_inconsistent`. A failing sum that pairing cannot place goes to `claude-sonnet-4.6`, which is shown
the sum in words and what has been tried, and answers with one JSON action: `reread` (one or more targets),
`cannot_verify` (a reason) or `done`. Code carries the action out and answers with the checks' new result. A model never
sets a status: a cell is accepted when every printed sum it sits on holds, and only then.

Rules that code enforces whatever the model says:
- at most MAX_ACTIONS actions per item (a refused request counts as one);
- the ladder: the county's reader first, then `claude-sonnet-4.6`, then `claude-opus-4.6`; a step is allowed on a target
  only after the step below has been tried on it (and failed to settle it); model names are matched after trimming and
  lower-casing, and an unknown name falls back to the next step of the ladder;
- the same target is never re-read twice with the same model and dpi (a refusal, and it counts as an action);
- a cell that is already accepted is never re-read; a total is re-read only while a sum it sits on fails;
- a re-read value replaces the old one only if more of that value's sums hold with it; both readings are kept in the event;
- when an item stops, only the cells that pairing or the model could not clear become cannot_verify (a cell whose other
  sum holds is not marked); every sum still failing at the end has a verdict and a reason.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import json
import time
from dataclasses import dataclass, field
from pathlib import Path

from . import checks, tracing
from .layouts.matrix import ROWS, GeometryError, digit_px, scale_for  # noqa: F401  (re-exported for callers)
from .model import BudgetExceeded

HAIKU = "claude-haiku"
SONNET = "claude-sonnet-4.6"
OPUS = "claude-opus-4.6"
DECIDER = SONNET          # the model that chooses what to look at for sums pairing cannot place
MAX_ACTIONS = 6
DPIS = (300, 400, 500, 600)
SUSPECT_DPI = 400
STRIP_CELLS = 7           # a row strip is cut into pieces of at most this many cells
KINDS = ("cell", "column", "row_total", "col_total", "grand", "row_strip")
SUM_KINDS = ("row", "col", "grand_col", "grand_row")
FINAL = ("cannot_verify", "document_inconsistent")
ORDER = {"row": 0, "col": 1, "grand_col": 2, "grand_row": 3}


def norm(name) -> str:
    return str(name or "").strip().lower()


def ladder_for(reader: str) -> list[str]:
    """The reader of the county first, then the stronger models above it, each once."""
    out = [norm(reader) or HAIKU]
    for m in (SONNET, OPUS):
        if m not in out:
            out.append(m)
    return out


def pick_model(name, ladder: list[str], tried: set) -> tuple[int | None, str | None]:
    """(step, None) for the ladder step to use, or (None, reason) when the request is refused. `tried` holds the steps
    already used on this target. A name that is not on the ladder falls back to the lowest step not yet tried."""
    names = [norm(m) for m in ladder]
    n = norm(name)
    if n in names:
        i = names.index(n)
    else:
        i = next((j for j in range(len(names)) if j not in tried), len(names) - 1)
    if i > 0 and (i - 1) not in tried:
        return None, (f"{ladder[i]} is allowed on a target only after {ladder[i - 1]} has been tried on it "
                      "and failed to settle the value")
    return i, None


@dataclass
class Item:
    kind: str                 # 'row' | 'col' | 'grand_col' | 'grand_row': the kind of failing sum
    page: int
    block: str
    key: str
    actions: int = 0
    history: list = field(default_factory=list)

    @property
    def id(self) -> str:
        return f"{self.kind}:{self.page}:{self.block}:{self.key}"


def sum_id(ch) -> str:
    return f"{ch.kind}:{ch.page}:{ch.block_id}:{ch.key}"


def entity_of(key: tuple) -> tuple:
    """A checks entity key as the settle()/ledger entity: a cell key or a printed total."""
    return ("total", *key) if key[2] in ("row", "col", "grand") else ("cell", *key)


def target_of(key: tuple) -> dict:
    """The re-read target that shows one value: a cell, a row's printed total, a small total or the grand total."""
    page, block, x, y = key
    if x == "row":
        return {"kind": "row_total", "row": y}
    if x == "col":
        return {"kind": "col_total", "column": y}
    if x == "grand":
        return {"kind": "grand"}
    return {"kind": "cell", "row": x, "column": y}


def tkey(t: dict) -> str:
    return json.dumps(t, sort_keys=True)


# ---- state from the ledger -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

def _state(led, county):
    cells, totals = led.cells(county), led.totals(county)
    return cells, totals, checks.all_checks(cells, totals)


def _ck(ch) -> tuple:
    return (ch.kind, ch.page, ch.block_id, ch.key)


def _ckey(c) -> tuple:
    return checks.cell_key(c)


def derive_status(led, county) -> list[dict]:
    """Set every cell's status from the checks: accepted iff it sits on at least one printed sum and all hold.
    cannot_verify and document_inconsistent are final. Returns the changes [{cell, old, new}]."""
    cells, totals = led.cells(county), led.totals(county)
    on = checks.crossing(cells, totals)
    out = []
    for c in cells:
        if c["status"] in FINAL:
            continue
        cs = on.get(_ckey(c), [])
        new = "accepted" if cs and all(x.ok for x in cs) else ("failed" if c["status"] == "failed" else "first_read")
        if new != c["status"]:
            led.set_status(county, c["page"], c["block_id"], c["row_kind"], c["column"], new)
            out.append({"cell": list(_ckey(c)), "old": c["status"], "new": new})
    return out


def count_failing(chs) -> dict:
    """Failing sums by kind: grand = the small totals against the grand total (as in T03a), grand_row = the row totals."""
    out = {"row": 0, "col": 0, "grand": 0, "grand_row": 0}
    for ch in chs:
        out["grand" if ch.kind == "grand_col" else ch.kind] += not ch.ok
    return out


def _holding(entity, cells, totals) -> int:
    """How many printed sums that this cell or total sits on hold, given the lists as they are."""
    chs = checks.all_checks(cells, totals)
    if entity[0] == "cell":
        _, page, bid, row, col = entity
        return sum(ch.ok for ch in chs if ch.kind in ("row", "col") and ch.page == page and ch.block_id == bid and
                   any(k == (page, bid, row, col) for k, _ in ch.terms))
    _, page, bid, direction, key = entity
    return sum(ch.ok for ch in chs if ch.page == page and ch.block_id == bid and (
        (direction == "row" and ch.kind == "row" and ch.key == key) or
        (direction == "col" and ((ch.kind == "col" and ch.key == key) or ch.kind == "grand_col")) or
        (direction == "row" and ch.kind == "grand_row") or
        (direction == "grand" and ch.kind in ("grand_col", "grand_row"))))


def settle(led, county, updates: list[dict], seen: dict | None = None) -> list[dict]:
    """Decide for each proposed new value whether it replaces the old one: it does only if more of the sums it sits on
    hold with it than with the old value, the other proposed values being taken as they are. Writes the kept values.
    Each update: {entity: ('cell', page, block, row, col) | ('total', page, block, direction, key), old, new}.
    `seen` maps an entity to the values earlier re-reads gave it. Returns the updates with 'kept' ('new' | 'old' |
    'same') added."""
    cells, totals = led.cells(county), led.totals(county)

    def with_values(chosen):
        cs = [dict(c) for c in cells]
        ts = [dict(t) for t in totals]
        for u, v in chosen:
            e = u["entity"]
            if e[0] == "cell":
                for c in cs:
                    if _ckey(c) == tuple(e[1:]):
                        c["value"] = v
            else:
                for t in ts:
                    if (t["page"], t["block_id"], t["direction"], t["key"]) == tuple(e[1:]):
                        t["value"] = v
        return cs, ts

    live = [u for u in updates if u["new"] is not None and u["new"] != u["old"]]
    all_new = [(u, u["new"]) for u in live]
    for u in updates:
        if u not in live:
            u["kept"] = "same"
            continue
        reverted = [(x, x["old"] if x is u else x["new"]) for x in live]
        n_new = _holding(u["entity"], *with_values(all_new))
        n_old = _holding(u["entity"], *with_values(reverted))

def _int(v, what):
    if isinstance(v, int) and not isinstance(v, bool):
        return v
    raise ValueError(f"{what} must be an integer, got {v!r}")


def read_validator(kind, n=None):
    def check(d):
        if not isinstance(d, dict):
            raise ValueError("answer must be an object")
        if kind == "row_strip":
            v = d.get("values")
            if not isinstance(v, list) or len(v) != n:
                raise ValueError(f"values must be a list of {n} entries")
            for x in v:
                if x is not None:
                    _int(x, "value")
        elif kind == "column":
            for k in (*ROWS, "total"):
                _int(d.get(k), k)
        else:
            _int(d.get("value"), "value")
    return check


def decision_validator(d):
    if not isinstance(d, dict) or d.get("action") not in ("reread", "cannot_verify", "done"):
        raise ValueError('"action" must be "reread", "cannot_verify" or "done"')
    if d["action"] == "cannot_verify" and not str(d.get("reason") or "").strip():
        raise ValueError('"cannot_verify" needs a "reason"')
    if d["action"] != "reread":
        return
    rr = d.get("rereads")
    if rr is None and "target" in d:
        rr = [{k: d[k] for k in ("target", "dpi", "model") if k in d}]
    if not isinstance(rr, list) or not rr:
        raise ValueError('"reread" needs a non-empty "rereads" list')
    norm = []
    for r in rr:
        t = r.get("target") if isinstance(r, dict) else None
        if not isinstance(t, dict) or t.get("kind") not in KINDS:
            raise ValueError(f"target kind must be one of {KINDS}")
        need = {"cell": ("row", "column"), "column": ("column",), "row_total": ("row",), "col_total": ("column",),
                "grand": (), "row_strip": ("row",)}[t["kind"]]
        for f in need:
            if not isinstance(t.get(f), str) or not t[f]:
                raise ValueError(f'target {t["kind"]} needs "{f}"')
        dpi = r.get("dpi", 300)
        if dpi not in DPIS:
            raise ValueError(f"dpi must be one of {DPIS}")
        model = r.get("model") or ""
        if not isinstance(model, str):
            raise ValueError("model must be a name")
        norm.append({"target": {k: t[k] for k in ("kind", *need)}, "dpi": dpi, "model": model})  # unknown names: pick_model
    d["rereads"] = norm

"""The investigation loop's rules, with a fake model and a fake page. No network, no images of real scans."""
import json

import pytest
from PIL import Image

from crossfoot import agent, outputs, tracing
from crossfoot.ledger import Ledger

ROWS = ("EARLY", "ABSENTEE", "PRECINCT")
GOOD = {"1": (10, 2, 3), "2": (20, 4, 6)}     # column -> EARLY, ABSENTEE, PRECINCT
HAIKU, SONNET = "claude-haiku", "claude-sonnet-4.6"


def make_block(led, page, bid, good=GOOD, wrong=None, row_totals=None, col_totals=None, grand=None):
    """A block whose printed totals are those of `good`; `wrong` maps (row, column) -> the value the first read gave."""
    wrong = wrong or {}
    for col, vals in good.items():
        for r, v in zip(ROWS, vals):
            led.put_cell("x", page, bid, r, col, wrong.get((r, col), v), contest="C", candidate=f"cand {bid}")
        led.put_total("x", page, bid, "col", col, (col_totals or {}).get(col, sum(vals)))
    for i, r in enumerate(ROWS):
        led.put_total("x", page, bid, "row", r, (row_totals or {}).get(r, sum(v[i] for v in good.values())))
    led.put_total("x", page, bid, "grand", "", grand if grand is not None else sum(sum(v) for v in good.values()))


class FakeGeo:
    def __init__(self):
        self.targets = []

    def crop(self, page, bid, target, dpi, dest):
        self.targets.append((bid, dict(target), dpi))
        dest.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        Image.new("L", (10, 10), 255).save(dest)
        return dest, (0, 0, 10, 10)

    def total_box(self, page, bid, direction, key):
        return None

    def block_box(self, page, bid):
        return None


class FakeGw:
    """Decisions come from `decide(prompt, n)`, re-reads from `read(target, model, n)`. Logs every call."""
    def __init__(self, geo, decide, read, model=HAIKU):
        self.geo, self.decide, self.read, self.model = geo, decide, read, model
        self.calls = self.prompt_tokens = self.completion_tokens = 0
        self.cost = 0.0
        self.log = []

    def ask_json(self, prompt, image=None, *, validate=None, model=None):
        self.calls += 1
        model = model or self.model
        if image is None:
            ans = self.decide(prompt, sum(1 for m, k, _ in self.log if k == "decide"))
            self.log.append((model, "decide", prompt))
        else:
            bid, target, dpi = self.geo.targets[-1]
            ans = self.read(bid, target, model, sum(1 for m, k, _ in self.log if k == "read"))
            self.log.append((model, "read", (bid, target, dpi)))
        if validate:
            validate(ans)
        return ans


def reread_col(col, model=HAIKU, dpi=300):
    return {"action": "reread", "rereads": [{"target": {"kind": "column", "column": col}, "dpi": dpi, "model": model}]}


def truth_reader(good=GOOD):
    def read(bid, t, model, n):
        if t["kind"] == "column":
            e, a, p = good[t["column"]]
            return {"EARLY": e, "ABSENTEE": a, "PRECINCT": p, "total": e + a + p}
        if t["kind"] == "cell":
            return {"value": good[t["column"]][ROWS.index(t["row"])]}
        raise AssertionError(t)
    return read
